scene: four dark round loaves left on a wooden bakery counter under a glass shelf, a small hand-lettered card propped against the front one, wire cooling racks and a scatter of flour on the boards, brown paper bags folded in a stack at the edge, a set of tongs, warm late afternoon light coming in low from a shop window

the floor of a beech wood in early may seen low and along, bluebells running unbroken between the trunks and over a slight rise, one fallen branch lying across the drift, last year's leaf litter showing through in patches, a thin desire path worn to bare earth, green light coming down through new leaves

nine ring binders and card folders stacked at angles in a canvas bag on a kitchen floor, tabs and sugar paper corners sticking out of them at different heights, a red pen and a bulldog clip on the tiles beside the bag, one folder slipped free and lying flat with a photocopied grid sheet on top, hard morning light from a window off frame

a paper timetable pinned to a weathered green noticeboard by a flight of stone river steps, four drawing pins and one corner already curling, the printed grid of times legible as pattern rather than text, a rusted hook screwed into the frame below with three more copies hanging from it, flat bright overcast light and a smear of rain on the perspex

a small dental waiting room seen from a chair, a rectangular fish tank on a low table with two fish and a plastic castle in blue gravel, a rack of folded leaflets on the wall behind it, four grey stacking chairs and a low table with magazines squared into a pile, strip lighting and a carpet worn pale in a track to the door

a wide bowl of very pale green soup on a steel kitchen bench, the surface flat and matt with a few darker fronds dropped on top and a thread of oil, the heavy enamel pan behind it with the lid leaning against the base, a torn heel of dark bread on the bench beside a spoon laid handle out, one bare bulb overhead and a dark window

an open sketchbook page carrying a soft pencil drawing of a fish tank with a plastic castle in it, the castle drawn slightly too large and slightly too straight, gravel done as hundreds of small marks, water suggested by an eraser lift across the whole page, the facing page blank with a pencil laid in the gutter, warm lamp light from the right

a new dark passport lying closed on a kitchen table with the torn courier envelope beneath it, a stiff card insert half slid out, the old passport with its corner clipped lying alongside at an angle, a bunch of keys and a cold mug at the top edge of the frame, grey even daylight from a window to the left

a small table under a lamp with a fat ring binder open near the back of it, three pages torn out and squared in a row, a pencil laid parallel to the pages, a glass of water and a bus card with a printed number on it, the lamp pushed hard to one side so the light falls flat across the paper, dark flat behind

an open paper of chips resting on worn stone river steps, the paper folded back at the corners and going translucent, a wooden fork stuck upright in them, a torn sachet and two loose chips on the stone, the green river water and a mooring chain in the background out of focus, hard bright afternoon light

a hawthorn hedge in full flower along a rough lane at the top of a towpath, the whole length of it gone white at once and already dropping petals onto the ruts, a leaning wooden post with two strands of wire, the flat green fields beyond, warm hazy late morning light
